an3.50:1.1: “Bhikkhus, possessing three factors, a master thief breaks into houses, plunders wealth, commits banditry, and ambushes highways.
an3.50:1.3: Here, a master thief depends on the uneven, on thickets, and on powerful people.
an3.50:1.4: (1) “And how does a master thief depend on the uneven?
an3.50:1.5: Here, a master thief depends on rivers that are hard to cross and rugged mountains.
an3.50:1.6: It is in this way that a master thief depends on the uneven.
an3.50:2.2: (2) “And how does a master thief depend on thickets? Here, a master thief depends on a thicket of cane, a thicket of trees, a coppice, or a large dense jungle.
an3.50:2.3: It is in this way that a master thief depends on thickets.
an3.50:3.1: (3) “And how does a master thief depend on powerful people?
an3.50:3.2: Here, a master thief depends on kings or royal ministers.
an3.50:3.4: ‘If anyone accuses me of anything, these kings or royal ministers will dismiss the case.’ If anyone accuses him of anything, those kings or royal ministers dismiss the case.
an3.50:3.6: It is in this way that a master thief depends on powerful people.
an3.50:3.7: “It is by possessing these three factors that a master thief breaks into houses, plunders wealth, commits banditry, and ambushes highways.
an3.50:4.1: “So too, bhikkhus, possessing three qualities, an evil bhikkhu maintains himself in a maimed and injured condition, is blameworthy and subject to reproach by the wise, and generates much demerit.
an3.50:4.3: Here, an evil bhikkhu depends on the uneven, on thickets, and on powerful people.
an3.50:5.1: (1) “And how does an evil bhikkhu depend on the uneven?
an3.50:5.2: Here, an evil bhikkhu engages in unrighteous bodily, verbal, and mental action.
an3.50:5.3: It is in this way that an evil bhikkhu depends on the uneven.
an3.50:6.1: (2) “And how does an evil bhikkhu depend on thickets?
an3.50:6.2: Here, an evil bhikkhu holds wrong view, adopts an extremist view.
an3.50:6.3: It is in this way that an evil bhikkhu depends on thickets.
an3.50:7.1: (3) “And how does an evil bhikkhu depend on powerful people?
an3.50:7.2: Here, an evil bhikkhu depends on kings or royal ministers.
an3.50:7.4: ‘If anyone accuses me of anything, these kings or royal ministers will dismiss the case.’ If anyone accuses him of anything, those kings or royal ministers dismiss the case.
an3.50:7.6: It is in this way that an evil bhikkhu depends on the powerful.
an3.50:7.7: “It is by possessing these three qualities that an evil bhikkhu maintains himself in a maimed and injured condition, is blameworthy and subject to reproach by the wise, and generates much demerit.”
